evidence.summary: MAX_BYTES = 10 MB; comment says uploads over 10 MB are rejected.
upload() raises ValueError('file too large') above MAX_BYTES, else store.save(owner_id, name, size, data).
list_files() returns store.list(owner_id) - files scoped to one owner.
delete_file() calls store.delete(owner_id, file_id) - delete scoped by owner.
Table files(id text pk, owner_id text not null, name text not null, size integer not null, created_at timestamp not null); no column for file bytes.
Docstring calls the module illustrative; the store object it calls is not in the source, so storage and HTTP layer are unknown.

architecture.backend: plain Python functions over an injected store object; no HTTP layer in the source

features.name: Upload a file
features.description: Owner uploads a named file; it is stored with its size.
features.observed_behaviour: len(data) > 10 MB raises ValueError('file too large'); otherwise store.save is called with owner_id, name, size and data and its result returned.
features.business_logic: Max size 10 * 1024 * 1024 bytes (exactly 10 MB is allowed).
features.integration: needs an owner identity (auth) and file storage

features.name: List my files
features.description: Owner lists the files they uploaded.
features.business_logic: Only the owner's files are returned.

features.name: Delete my file
features.description: Owner deletes one of their files.
features.observed_behaviour: Calls store.delete(owner_id, file_id); behaviour for a missing or foreign file depends on the store, which is not in the source.
features.integration: needs an owner identity; share links to a deleted file should stop working

unknowns: The store implementation (save/list/delete) is not in the source: id generation, where file bytes live (schema.sql has no data column) and missing/foreign-file behaviour on delete are unknown; the store code would settle it.
No authentication or user model: owner_id is passed in by the caller; how it is obtained is unknown.
No HTTP/UI layer: routes and screens do not exist in this source.
